title: What Abundance Logistics Networks Is
definition: Abundance Logistics Networks: logistics for a world of plenty.
description:
Strip Abundance Logistics Networks to its essence and you get logistics for a world of plenty. Simple to say, civilizational to build.

The path runs through Post-Scarcity Economy: first surplus routing understanding, then network logistics prototypes, then waste prevention operations at scale. Each stage has its own physics, its own economics, and its own failure modes — this database maps all three.

Use the ladder: start with foundations, work through the components and forecasts, run every demo, then attempt the compounded drills. By the final record you will hold a working mental model of network hulls, grounded in real research and honest about what remains unknown.

t: Real Research Today: Abundance Logistics Networks
title: Real Research Today: Abundance Logistics Networks
definition: Today's documented research behind Abundance Logistics Networks.
description:
The road to Abundance Logistics Networks is already being paved. The Maricá (Brazil) basic income and Spain's ingreso mínimo vital are large public pilots. Platform cooperativism (Trebor Scholz) builds worker-owned digital platforms.

Time-banking networks (TimeBanks USA) trade hours as currency in hundreds of communities. Together these programs form the surplus routing foundation that Abundance Logistics Networks will build on — the network logistics results, the waste prevention methods, and the institutional memory.

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as network logistics research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

definition: 2030 milestone on the Abundance Logistics Networks roadmap.
description:
First city-scale network hulls pilots launch: surplus routing issuance and network logistics exchange running live.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed surplus routing demonstrations, network logistics cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting waste prevention uptime. When all three flash green, 2030 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (4 years from the 2026 baseline.)

title: Readiness Estimator: Abundance Logistics Networks
definition: Estimates Abundance Logistics Networks readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Abundance Logistics Networks components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a network hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

definition: Simulates Abundance Logistics Networks operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Abundance Logistics Networks installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 24059 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where surplus routing monitoring, network logistics redundancy, or waste prevention maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Abundance Logistics Networks Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Abundance Logistics Networks: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Abundance Logistics Networks — logistics for a world of plenty.

Phase 1 — Prove (surplus routing): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (network logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (waste prevention): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (sharing hubs): network hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and cities-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
